provider_note: Deliberately provider-oriented but free of PostHog insight/dashboard IDs: those are unstable and would rot faster than the definitions. Rebuild insights from the fields below.

opted_in_install.description: One random UUIDv4 distinct_id that has sent at least one product event. NOT a person and NOT every user — telemetry is opt-in, so all product metrics are a lower bound.
opted_in_install.distinct_id: random UUIDv4 generated on the machine at opt-in

distribution_metrics.description: Scheduled collector rows. Constant distinct_id 'distribution_metrics'. Never mix into user cohorts.

role_resolution.rule: RESOLVE ROLE PER asset_id FIRST: asset_role is a label on a row, not part of the asset's identity — asset_id is. Take the role from each asset_id's MOST RECENT snapshot, then aggregate over ALL of that asset_id's rows regardless of the role recorded on older ones. Filtering rows by asset_role and aggregating within the filtered set splits a reclassified asset in two.
role_resolution.why: Roles were reclassified on 2026-08-27 (see role_reclassification). Rows already in PostHog keep their old label, so a reclassified asset_id has rows under two different asset_role values.
wrong_and_what_it_produces: filter asset_role='plugin_manifest', then first = MAX(value) where observed_date <= period_start else 0 -> no pre-cutover row survives the filter, first falls back to 0, and the asset's ENTIRE lifetime counter is reported as period traffic (measured: 3387 instead of 5)
filter asset_role='plugin' over a window spanning the cutover -> the manifest's pre-cutover growth is counted as plugin package downloads (measured: 382 instead of 0)
role_resolution.note: A date filter does NOT fix this. Scoping to observed_date >= cutover is exactly what makes the baseline fall back to 0.

engaged_events_note: app_started is deliberately excluded: launching the app is not usage, and including it is the easiest way to make retention look better than the product is.

metrics.caveat: An install that opts in after weeks of use enters the cohort on the day we first saw it, which biases this upward. For a clean number restrict the cohort to installs whose first app_started and telemetry_enabled are within 24h of each other, and say which variant you reported.

metrics.title: GitHub installer downloads (lifetime)
metrics.query_note: RESOLVE ROLE PER asset_id FIRST: asset_role is a label on a row, not part of the asset's identity — asset_id is. Take the role from each asset_id's MOST RECENT snapshot, then aggregate over ALL of that asset_id's rows regardless of the role recorded on older ones. Filtering rows by asset_role and aggregating within the filtered set splits a reclassified asset in two. download_count_total is a CUMULATIVE counter snapshotted daily. Take MAX per asset_id, then sum across asset_ids. Summing snapshot rows multiplies the number by the number of collection days. Per-asset MAX also preserves history for assets that were deleted or replaced.
metrics.not: not users; not installs; excludes updater/update_check/checksum/wheel/sdist/plugin/plugin_manifest roles on purpose

metrics.title: GitHub installer downloads (30d)
metrics.query_note: RESOLVE ROLE PER asset_id FIRST: asset_role is a label on a row, not part of the asset's identity — asset_id is. Take the role from each asset_id's MOST RECENT snapshot, then aggregate over ALL of that asset_id's rows regardless of the role recorded on older ones. Filtering rows by asset_role and aggregating within the filtered set splits a reclassified asset in two. per asset_id: last = MAX(value) where observed_date <= period_end; first = MAX(value) where observed_date <= period_start else 0; delta = max(0, last - first); then sum. Baseline 0 makes a release published mid-period contribute all of its downloads; max(0,...) guards a replaced asset whose counter appears to move backwards.

disclaimer: Product metrics cover opted-in anonymous installs only and are a lower bound on real usage. Download counts are public distribution counts, not users.

Distribution / Downloads.description: Someone made a deliberate choice to fetch this. Only these may be called downloads — and even here a download is not a user.

Infrastructure / Automated Traffic.description: Machines fetching things on a schedule. Nobody chose any of this. These belong on the dashboard for operational reasons ONLY and must never appear under Downloads, Users, or Installs.
Infrastructure / Automated Traffic.hard_rule: No metric in this section may be summed into a Distribution / Downloads total, a user count, or an install count.

role_reclassification.what_changed: latest.json moved from role 'updater' to 'update_check'; codex-plugin.json moved from role 'plugin' to 'plugin_manifest'.
role_reclassification.why: Both are polled by machines. Measured on 2026-08-27: codex-plugin.json accounted for 3382 of 3387 requests in the old 'plugin' role (99.85%), and latest.json for 44 of 66 in the old 'updater' role.
role_reclassification.query_impact: Rows already in PostHog are NOT retroactively reclassified, so a reclassified asset_id has rows under two asset_role values. Do NOT filter rows by asset_role and aggregate within the filtered set, and do NOT try to fix it with a date filter — see role_resolution. Resolve each asset_id's role from its latest snapshot, then aggregate over all of that asset_id's rows.
role_reclassification.expected_artifact: 'Plugin package downloads' drops from ~3378 to ~5 on the changeover date. That is the fix landing, not a regression.
